messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: getting started on bbbb
parts:
I'm around, but don't know how to run variational inference.
So I'm forwarding to stan-dev, where this kind of question
should go.

Alp or Dustin should be able to point you at the branch
on CmdStan where variational inference is implemented. Hopefully
you will be able to build the manual and look at the doc on how
to run it. If not, the first order of business is writing the
doc so that it can be followed. This is why it's good to have
people other than the authors try it out. So thanks.

- Bob

> I went over Matt's paper on stochastic VB and Rajesh's paper on Black box VB (yet to start with alp's paper).
>
> Just wanted to know if its worth investing more time in stochastic optimization in general, I don't know if its a widely used technique. Also, I found a nice extension of SVI for hidden markov models.
>
> See you tomorrow!
>

> to be tied to OS updates.
>
> You're right --- we haven't built the interface
> for variational inference in RStan yet.
>
> Alp's paper's a tough third read in variational
> inference! It's pretty much presupposing Rajesh's
> paper on black-box VB and Matt's paper on stochastic
> VB, so those may be better papers to read after Bishop
> and Gelman et al. --- they'll be in the references.
>
> - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] getting started on bbbb
parts:
I showed Jalaj how to run it in person a few days ago. For anyone curious, using variational inference is available in the feature/advi-command branch of cmdstan. Alp wrote the documentation in the manual which you can compile. I’m also happy to help anyone who is having issues with it! (just respond on this thread or in the stan-users mailing list)

Dustin
